films.title: Telemetry strategy and budget
films.description: A short narrated film on telemetry strategy and budget across hundreds of teams: three-store stacks vs observability 2.0 wide events, limits per team and cost attribution.

films.title: Telemetry pipeline as a platform
films.description: A short narrated film on running OpenTelemetry Collectors as a tier-0 platform service: processor order, queue loss, SLOs and OpAMP.

films.title: Prometheus topology: shards, HA and remote write
films.description: A short narrated film on scaling Prometheus across hundreds of clusters: discovery, relabeling, WAL, HA pairs, remote write and fleet SLIs.

films.title: Query and rule standards for the fleet
films.description: A short narrated film on fleet PromQL standards: rate before sum, histograms, recording-rule libraries, Sloth SLO generation and promtool CI tests.

films.title: Trace propagation as a fleet standard
films.description: A short narrated film on distributed trace propagation across hundreds of services: W3C traceparent, queues, broken proxies, OTel Operator defaults and completeness.

films.title: Org sampling policy: head and tail
films.description: Who sets the org sampling policy, how head and tail sampling fit together, and how to prove cost and fidelity per team.

films.title: Log standards: schema, labels and retention tiers
films.description: Canonical structured logs, Loki label allowlists vs structured metadata, node-agent drops, retention tiers, and per-tenant billing.

films.title: Paging as an org control loop
films.description: Multi-window SLO burn rates, HA Alertmanager deduplication, routing and inhibition, pager budgets, and org responses when a team goes over.

films.title: Observability when agents do the reading
films.description: Wide correlated events, OBI eBPF v1.0, OTel profiles alpha, owned Collector pipelines, read-only MCP identities, hard query limits, and GenAI spans.

films.title: CI as a shared service
films.description: One pull request's path through a CI shared by 2,000 engineers: queue time, runners, cache, parallel tests, OIDC, flaky checks and the merge queue.

films.title: Build once, promote everywhere
films.description: A short narrated film: build one image, deploy the same digest to dev, staging and production, and keep the previous digest for rollback.

films.title: Desired-state control across hundreds of clusters
films.description: A short narrated film on running Argo CD across hundreds of clusters: sync, drift as a fleet metric, and a written break-glass policy.

films.title: Rollout policy as a platform default
films.description: How a platform makes metric-gated canary rollout the default for every service, and measures how much of the fleet uses it.

films.title: Flag governance
films.description: A short narrated film on running thousands of feature flags: staged flips, a tier 0 flag service, safe defaults, expiry dates and a per-team scorecard.

films.title: Schema-change safety
films.description: How expand and contract, migration lint, role timeouts, a queue and a drop gate keep shared schema changes safe and rollback possible.

films.title: Supply chain: provenance, signing and SBOMs
films.description: How to prove every image running in production was built by your CI from a reviewed commit, and keep everything else out.

films.title: Merge queues, monorepos and DORA
films.description: How a merge queue keeps one busy main branch green and deployable, and how DORA metrics show whether delivery is improving.

films.title: Trunk-based delivery without a blocking review
films.description: When review stops blocking the merge, where each job the pull request did goes: authorization, test gates, the second look and the record.

films.title: Review lanes set by risk
films.description: A short narrated film on how a lane policy sends each change to no, one or two human reviewers by risk, and how each lane is measured.

films.title: What an agent actually is
films.description: A coding agent is a model, tools and a loop run by a harness. Eleven short scenes on what a platform team controls around it.

films.title: Context engineering
films.description: How rules, skills, tools and code reach a coding agent's context window, and how a platform keeps that context short and current.

films.title: Verification first: go deep, then prove it
films.description: A narrated walk through the trust loop for coding agents: reproduce, prove the cause, fix small, then show evidence a check the agent can't edit accepts.

films.title: Orchestrating many agents
films.description: How to split work across many coding agents, keep them from overwriting each other, and bound what lands on main.

films.title: Reviewing agent output
films.description: How an org keeps code review meaningful when agents open more pull requests than reviewers can read.

films.title: Permissions and safety for coding agents
films.description: A four-minute narrated film of the Agentic Engineering chapter on permissions and safety for coding agents: sandboxes, egress, scoped credentials and a second model that reviews each action.

films.title: Agents in SRE operations
films.description: What an incident agent may do alone, and how an alert class earns autonomy: read-only identity, dry runs, approvals, traces and replays.

films.title: Running agentic development across an org
films.description: A narrated walk through rolling out coding agents to 2,000 engineers: platform, eval gates, managed config, labels, spend and outcomes.

films.title: Evals: the asset that compounds most
films.description: Why an eval suite of your own real tasks gains value with every model release, and how it decides upgrades.

films.title: Upgrading models safely
films.description: A short narrated film: how to move hundreds of services off a retiring model with evals, a shadow run, a canary, and a pin you can move back.
